passages.text: Some time later there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon: Jesus is the Son of God.\r\nSome time later, the Jews held a feast.\r\nJesus went up to Jerusalem.
passages.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἦν ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων καὶ ἀνέβη Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα

passages.text: Now there is in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate a pool with five covered colonnades, which in Hebrew is called Bethesda.
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem is a city.
There is a gate in Jerusalem called the Sheep Gate.
Near the Sheep Gate, there is a pool.
The pool has five covered colonnades.
People call this pool Bethesda in Hebrew.
passages.original: Ἔστιν δὲ ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐπὶ τῇ προβατικῇ κολυμβήθρα ἡ ἐπιλεγομένη Ἑβραϊστὶ Βηθεσδά πέντε στοὰς ἔχουσα

passages.text: On these walkways lay a great number of the sick, the blind, the lame, and the paralyzed.
passages.sermon:
Many people were sick.
Many people were blind.
Many people could not walk.
Many people were paralyzed.
These people lay on the walkways near the pool in Jerusalem.
passages.original: ἐν ταύταις κατέκειτο πλῆθος τῶν ἀσθενούντων τυφλῶν χωλῶν ξηρῶν

passages.text: One man there had been an invalid for thirty-eight years.
passages.sermon:
A man was there.
He was sick.
He had been sick for thirty-eight years.
He was an invalid.
He stayed at the pool near the Sheep Gate in Jerusalem.
This pool was called Bethesda.
Many sick people lay there.
passages.original: Ἦν δέ τις ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ τριάκοντα καὶ ὀκτὼ ἔτη ἔχων ἐν τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: When Jesus saw him lying there and realized that he had spent a long time in this condition, He asked him, “Do you want to get well?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw the man lying there.
Jesus knew the man had been sick for a long time.
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus asked, “Do you want to get well?”
passages.original: τοῦτον ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς κατακείμενον καὶ γνοὺς ὅτι πολὺν ἤδη χρόνον ἔχει λέγει αὐτῷ Θέλεις ὑγιὴς γενέσθαι

passages.text: “Sir,” the invalid replied, “I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am on my way, someone else goes in before me.”
passages.sermon:
A man lay there.
He had been an invalid for thirty-eight years.
Jesus spoke to him.
Jesus asked if he wanted to be well.
The man answered Jesus.
He said, “Sir, I have no one to help me.”
He said, “When the water is stirred, I cannot get into the pool.”
He said, “While I am going, someone else goes in before me.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ ὁ ἀσθενῶν Κύριε ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἔχω ἵνα ὅταν ταραχθῇ τὸ ὕδωρ βάλῃ με εἰς τὴν κολυμβήθραν ἐν ᾧ δὲ ἔρχομαι ἐγὼ ἄλλος πρὸ ἐμοῦ καταβαίνει

passages.text: Then Jesus told him, “Get up, pick up your mat, and walk.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a man who had been sick for a long time.
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus said, “Get up.”
Jesus said, “Pick up your mat.”
Jesus said, “Walk.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἔγειρε ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει

passages.text: Immediately the man was made well, and he picked up his mat and began to walk. Now this happened on the Sabbath day, so the Jews said to the man who had been healed, “This is the Sabbath! It is unlawful for you to carry your mat.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed a man who had been an invalid.
Immediately, the man became well.
The man picked up his mat.
The man began to walk.
This happened on the Sabbath day.
The Jews saw the man who had been healed.
The Jews said to him, “This is the Sabbath.”
The Jews said, “It is not lawful for you to carry your mat.”
passages.original: Καὶ εὐθέως ἐγένετο ὑγιὴς ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἦρεν τὸν κράβαττον αὐτοῦ καὶ περιεπάτει Ἦν δὲ σάββατον ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τῷ τεθεραπευμένῳ Σάββατόν ἐστιν καὶ οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἆραι τὸν κράβαττον σου

passages.text: But he answered, “The man who made me well told me, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’ ”
passages.sermon: The healed man spoke to them.\r\nHe said, “The man who made me well told me this.\r\nHe said, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’”
passages.original: ὃς δὲ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς Ὁ ποιήσας με ὑγιῆ ἐκεῖνός μοι εἶπεν Ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει

passages.text: “Who is this man who told you to pick it up and walk?” they asked.
passages.sermon: The Jews spoke to the man who had been healed.\r\nThey asked him a question.\r\nThey said, “Who is the man who told you to pick up your mat and walk?”
passages.original: Ἠρώτησαν οὖν αὐτόν Τίς ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ εἰπών σοι Ἆρον καὶ περιπάτει

passages.text: But the man who was healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had slipped away while the crowd was there.
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed a man who had been sick.
The man did not know who healed him.
Jesus had left the place quietly.
A crowd was present at that place.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἰαθεὶς οὐκ ᾔδει τίς ἐστιν ὁ γὰρ Ἰησοῦς ἐξένευσεν ὄχλου ὄντος ἐν τῷ τόπῳ

passages.text: Afterward, Jesus found the man at the temple and said to him, “See, you have been made well. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus healed a man who had been sick.
Later, Jesus found this man at the temple.
Jesus spoke to the man.
Jesus said, “You are well now.”
Jesus said, “Do not sin anymore.”
Jesus warned, “If you sin, something worse may happen to you.”
passages.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα εὑρίσκει αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἴδε ὑγιὴς γέγονας μηκέτι ἁμάρτανε ἵνα μὴ χεῖρόν σοί τι γένηται

passages.text: And the man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
passages.sermon:
A man had been healed by Jesus.
The man left.
He went to the Jews.
He told the Jews that Jesus had made him well.
passages.original: ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἀνήγγειλεν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ ποιήσας αὐτὸν ὑγιῆ

passages.text: Now because Jesus was doing these things on the Sabbath, the Jews began to persecute Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus healed a man.
He did this on the Sabbath.
The Jews saw what Jesus did.
The Jews began to persecute Jesus.
They persecuted Him because He did these things on the Sabbath.
passages.original: Καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐδίωκον οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὅτι ταῦτα ἐποίει ἐν σαββάτῳ

passages.text: But Jesus answered them, “To this very day My Father is at His work, and I too am working.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the Jews.
Jesus answered them directly.
Jesus said, "My Father is working right now."
Jesus said, "I am also working."
Jesus showed that God is His Father.
Jesus showed that He works as His Father works.
Jesus made it clear that both He and His Father are always active.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτοῖς Ὁ Πατήρ μου ἕως ἄρτι ἐργάζεται κἀγὼ ἐργάζομαι

passages.text: Because of this, the Jews tried all the harder to kill Him. Not only was He breaking the Sabbath, but He was even calling God His own Father, making Himself equal with God.
passages.sermon:
The Jews tried even harder to kill Jesus.
They did this because Jesus was breaking the Sabbath.
Jesus also called God His own Father.
By doing this, Jesus made Himself equal with God.
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο οὖν μᾶλλον ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀποκτεῖναι ὅτι οὐ μόνον ἔλυεν τὸ σάββατον ἀλλὰ καὶ Πατέρα ἴδιον ἔλεγεν τὸν Θεόν ἴσον ἑαυτὸν ποιῶν τῷ Θεῷ

passages.text: So Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing by Himself, unless He sees the Father doing it. For whatever the Father does, the Son also does.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus said, “I tell you the truth.
The Son cannot do anything by Himself.
The Son only does what He sees the Father doing.
Whatever the Father does, the Son does the same.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίνατο οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν οὐ δύναται ὁ Υἱὸς ποιεῖν ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ οὐδὲν ἐὰν μή τι βλέπῃ τὸν Πατέρα ποιοῦντα ἃ γὰρ ἂν ἐκεῖνος ποιῇ ταῦτα καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς ὁμοίως ποιεῖ

passages.text: The Father loves the Son and shows Him all He does. And to your amazement, He will show Him even greater works than these.
passages.sermon:
God is the Father.
Jesus is the Son.
The Father loves the Son.
The Father shows the Son everything He does.
The Father will show the Son even greater works than these.
You will be amazed.
passages.original: ὁ γὰρ Πατὴρ φιλεῖ τὸν Υἱὸν καὶ πάντα δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ ἃ αὐτὸς ποιεῖ καὶ μείζονα τούτων δείξει αὐτῷ ἔργα ἵνα ὑμεῖς θαυμάζητε

passages.text: For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom He wishes.
passages.sermon:
God is the Father.
The Father raises dead people.
The Father gives life to the dead.
Jesus is the Son.
The Son gives life to people.
The Son chooses whom He gives life to.
The Son gives life just as the Father does.
passages.original: Ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐγείρει τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ ζωοποιεῖ οὕτως καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς οὓς θέλει ζωοποιεῖ

passages.text: Furthermore, the Father judges no one, but has assigned all judgment to the Son, so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.
passages.sermon:
God is the Father.
The Father sent the Son.
The Father does not judge anyone.
The Father has given all judgment to the Son.
The Father did this so that everyone will honor the Son.
People should honor the Son just as they honor the Father.
If someone does not honor the Son, he does not honor the Father.
The Father is the one who sent the Son.
passages.original: οὐδὲ γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ κρίνει οὐδένα ἀλλὰ τὴν κρίσιν πᾶσαν δέδωκεν τῷ Υἱῷ ἵνα πάντες τιμῶσι τὸν Υἱὸν καθὼς τιμῶσι τὸν Πατέρα ὁ μὴ τιμῶν τὸν Υἱὸν οὐ τιμᾷ τὸν Πατέρα τὸν πέμψαντα αὐτόν

passages.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears My word and believes Him who sent Me has eternal life and will not come under judgment. Indeed, he has crossed over from death to life.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the Son of God.
God the Father sent Jesus.
Jesus says, “Truly, truly, I tell you.”
Anyone who hears Jesus’ word has a choice.
Anyone who believes God the Father, who sent Jesus, receives something.
That person has eternal life.
That person will not come under judgment.
That person has crossed over from death to life.
passages.original: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὁ τὸν λόγον μου ἀκούων καὶ πιστεύων τῷ πέμψαντί με ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον καὶ εἰς κρίσιν οὐκ ἔρχεται ἀλλὰ μεταβέβηκεν ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου εἰς τὴν ζωήν

passages.text: Truly, truly, I tell you, the hour is coming and has now come when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus speaks with authority from God.
I tell you the truth.
The time is coming.
The time is now here.
The dead will hear the voice of the Son of God.
Those who hear will live.
passages.original: Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ νῦν ἐστιν ὅτε οἱ νεκροὶ ἀκούσουσιν τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀκούσαντες ζήσουσιν

passages.text: For as the Father has life in Himself, so also He has granted the Son to have life in Himself.
passages.sermon:
God is the Father.
The Father has life in Himself.
The Father gave the Son a special gift.
The Father granted the Son to have life in Himself.
The Son now has life in Himself, just as the Father does.
passages.original: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ ἔχει ζωὴν ἐν ἑαυτῷ οὕτως καὶ τῷ Υἱῷ ἔδωκεν ζωὴν ἔχειν ἐν ἑαυτῷ

passages.text: And He has given Him authority to execute judgment, because He is the Son of Man.
passages.sermon: God gave Jesus authority to judge.\r\nJesus is the Son of Man.\r\nGod gave Jesus this authority because Jesus is the Son of Man.
passages.original: καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ κρίσιν ποιεῖν ὅτι Υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν

passages.text: Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming when all who are in their graves will hear His voice and come out—those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
God the Father has given Jesus authority to judge.
Do not be amazed at this.
A time is coming.
All people who are in their graves will hear Jesus’ voice.
All these people will come out of their graves.
Those who have done good will rise to life.
Those who have done evil will rise to judgment.
passages.original: μὴ θαυμάζετε τοῦτο ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα ἐν ᾗ πάντες οἱ ἐν τοῖς μνημείοις ἀκούσουσιν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκπορεύσονται οἱ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ποιήσαντες εἰς ἀνάστασιν ζωῆς οἱ δὲ τὰ φαῦλα πράξαντες εἰς ἀνάστασιν κρίσεως

passages.text: I can do nothing by Myself; I judge only as I hear. And My judgment is just, because I do not seek My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus is the Son of Man.
God sent Jesus.
Jesus cannot do anything by Himself.
Jesus judges only as He hears.
Jesus’ judgment is just.
Jesus does not seek His own will.
Jesus seeks the will of God, who sent Him.
passages.original: Οὐ δύναμαι ἐγὼ ποιεῖν ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐδέν καθὼς ἀκούω κρίνω καὶ ἡ κρίσις ἡ ἐμὴ δικαία ἐστίν ὅτι οὐ ζητῶ τὸ θέλημα τὸ ἐμὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με

passages.text: If I testify about Myself, My testimony is not valid.
passages.sermon: Jesus is speaking.\r\nJesus says, "If I testify about Myself, My testimony is not valid."\r\nMy own testimony about Myself does not count as true.
passages.original: Ἐὰν ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ ἡ μαρτυρία μου οὐκ ἔστιν ἀληθής

passages.text: There is another who testifies about Me, and I know that His testimony about Me is valid.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus says someone else testifies about Him.
Jesus knows this testimony is true.
This testimony is about Jesus.
passages.original: ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ μαρτυρῶν περὶ ἐμοῦ καὶ οἶδα ὅτι ἀληθής ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία ἣν μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ

passages.text: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
passages.sermon: You sent messengers to John.\r\nJohn testified to the truth.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς ἀπεστάλκατε πρὸς Ἰωάννην καὶ μεμαρτύρηκεν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ

passages.text: Even though I do not accept human testimony, I say these things so that you may be saved.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus does not accept testimony from people.
Jesus says these things for a reason.
Jesus wants you to be saved.
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ παρὰ ἀνθρώπου τὴν μαρτυρίαν λαμβάνω ἀλλὰ ταῦτα λέγω ἵνα ὑμεῖς σωθῆτε

passages.text: John was a lamp that burned and gave light, and you were willing for a season to bask in his light.
passages.sermon:
John was a lamp.
John burned brightly.
John gave light.
You wanted to rejoice in his light.
You were willing to enjoy his light for a time.
passages.original: Ἐκεῖνος ἦν ὁ λύχνος ὁ καιόμενος καὶ φαίνων ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠθελήσατε ἀγαλλιαθῆναι πρὸς ὥραν ἐν τῷ φωτὶ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But I have testimony more substantial than that of John. For the works that the Father has given Me to accomplish—the very works I am doing—testify about Me that the Father has sent Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is speaking.
Jesus has testimony greater than John's testimony.
The Father gave Jesus works to finish.
Jesus is doing these works now.
These works testify about Jesus.
These works show that the Father sent Jesus.
passages.original: ἐγὼ δὲ ἔχω τὴν μαρτυρίαν μείζω τοῦ Ἰωάννου τὰ γὰρ ἔργα ἃ δέδωκέν μοι ὁ Πατὴρ ἵνα τελειώσω αὐτά αὐτὰ τὰ ἔργα ἃ ποιῶ μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ ὅτι ὁ Πατήρ με ἀπέσταλκεν

passages.text: And the Father who sent Me has Himself testified about Me. You have never heard His voice nor seen His form, nor does His word abide in you, because you do not believe the One He sent.
passages.sermon:
The Father sent Me.
The Father Himself has testified about Me.
You have never heard the Father’s voice.
You have never seen the Father’s form.
God’s word does not remain in you.
You do not believe the One the Father sent.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ πέμψας με Πατὴρ ἐκεῖνος μεμαρτύρηκεν περὶ ἐμοῦ οὔτε φωνὴν αὐτοῦ πώποτε ἀκηκόατε οὔτε εἶδος αὐτοῦ ἑωράκατε καὶ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔχετε ἐν ὑμῖν μένοντα ὅτι ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ἐκεῖνος τούτῳ ὑμεῖς οὐ πιστεύετε

passages.text: You pore over the Scriptures because you presume that by them you possess eternal life. These are the very words that testify about Me, yet you refuse to come to Me to have life.
passages.sermon:
You study the Scriptures carefully.
You believe the Scriptures give you eternal life.
The Scriptures speak about Me.
You do not want to come to Me.
You do not come to Me to have life.
passages.original: Ἐραυνᾶτε τὰς γραφάς ὅτι ὑμεῖς δοκεῖτε ἐν αὐταῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἔχειν καὶ ἐκεῖναί εἰσιν αἱ μαρτυροῦσαι περὶ ἐμοῦ καὶ οὐ θέλετε ἐλθεῖν πρός με ἵνα ζωὴν ἔχητε

passages.text: I do not accept glory from men, but I know you, that you do not have the love of God within you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said, "I do not accept glory from men."
Jesus said, "I know you."
Jesus said, "You do not have the love of God within you."
passages.original: Δόξαν παρὰ ἀνθρώπων οὐ λαμβάνω ἀλλὰ ἔγνωκα ὑμᾶς ὅτι τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐκ ἔχετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς

passages.text: I have come in My Father’s name, and you have not received Me; but if someone else comes in his own name, you will receive him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus speaks to the people.
Jesus comes in the name of His Father.
The people do not receive Jesus.
Another person may come in his own name.
The people will receive that other person.
passages.original: ἐγὼ ἐλήλυθα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Πατρός μου καὶ οὐ λαμβάνετέ με ἐὰν ἄλλος ἔλθῃ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τῷ ἰδίῳ ἐκεῖνον λήμψεσθε

passages.text: How can you believe if you accept glory from one another, yet do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
\r\nJesus saw that they wanted praise from each other.
\r\nThey accepted honor from other people.
\r\nThey did not look for honor from God.
\r\nGod is the only true God.
\r\nJesus asked them a question.
\r\nHe said, “How can you believe?”
\r\nHe meant, “You cannot believe if you want praise from people.”
\r\nHe also meant, “You do not seek the honor that comes from God.”
passages.original: πῶς δύνασθε ὑμεῖς πιστεῦσαι δόξαν παρὰ ἀλλήλων λαμβάνοντες καὶ τὴν δόξαν τὴν παρὰ τοῦ μόνου Θεοῦ οὐ ζητεῖτε

passages.text: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. Your accuser is Moses, in whom you have put your hope.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus said, “Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father.
Moses is the one who accuses you.
You have put your hope in Moses.”
passages.original: Μὴ δοκεῖτε ὅτι ἐγὼ κατηγορήσω ὑμῶν πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα ἔστιν ὁ κατηγορῶν ὑμῶν Μωϋσῆς εἰς ὃν ὑμεῖς ἠλπίκατε

passages.text: If you had believed Moses, you would believe Me, because he wrote about Me.
passages.sermon: Moses was a leader and prophet of Israel.\r\nHe wrote about Me.\r\nIf you had believed Moses, you would believe Me.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ ἐπιστεύετε Μωϋσεῖ ἐπιστεύετε ἂν ἐμοί περὶ γὰρ ἐμοῦ ἐκεῖνος ἔγραψεν

passages.text: But since you do not believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He said they did not believe what Moses wrote.
Moses was a prophet and leader of Israel.
He wrote important words from God.
Jesus asked a question.
He said, "If you do not believe Moses' writings, you will not believe My words."
Jesus showed that believing Moses is necessary to believe Him.
passages.original: εἰ δὲ τοῖς ἐκείνου γράμμασιν οὐ πιστεύετε πῶς τοῖς ἐμοῖς ῥήμασιν πιστεύσετε
